phrases.english: He could not cross the bridge
they flow into the river, which is crossed by a bridge

phrases.latin: Pontem trānsībimus et in alterā rīpā cēnābimus.
phrases.english: We’ll cross the bridge and have supper on the other bank.

phrases.latin: super templum Dīvī Augustī ponte trānsmissō Palātium Capitōliumque conjūnxit
phrases.english: he joined the Palatine to the Capitol with a bridge thrown over the temple of the Deified Augustus

phrases.latin: Per pontem trānsībimus; sub nōbīs vehicula currunt.
phrases.english: We’ll cross by the bridge; the cars go by underneath us.

phrases.latin: Dum pontem trānsīmus, manum mihi dā.
phrases.english: Give me your hand while we go over the bridge.
The ducks are swimming under the bridge.
Look, a little boat is gliding under the bridge.

phrases.latin: Is terminus sacrī profānīque: in superiōre parte nāvigāre tantum, īnfrā etiam natāre concessum.
phrases.english: That bridge is the boundary between sacred and common water: above it you may only go by boat; below it you may swim as well.

sources: Lewis & Short: pons
